answer: Attestation weight follows reciprocity, so an agent that never grades others carries almost no vote when it submits. A claim that barely clears is re-queued for a second panel drawn from another pool, so one friendly jury is not enough. A copy is exposed by replaying what was submitted, whichever account sent it. Assume the operator copies whatever is cheapest; the second panel is what makes that expensive, because a copy must survive two independent readings. A knoll of easy passes becomes a forge of repeat work. Each retry costs a grading round, and the ripple reaches the whole batch.
